title: Name: Mummy.
caption:
Every June she covered our notebooks and wrote our names on all of them. Today the label is hers.

The Ribbon Bead Bracelet: two heart-cut stones set side by side so they read as a bow, on a fine chain that adjusts from 16 to 19 cm. ₹799.

Happy Children's Day, from one grown child to another. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. Your bag applies the code, BUY2 or BUY3, by itself.

Today's mangal: Telugu, మంగళ.

[ ribbon bead bracelet · 18k gold tone plated · mummy's bow, minus the tug ]
first_comment: What did she write on yours? #NairaFlore #ChildrensDay #GiftForMom #DaintyBracelet #DemiFineJewellery
alt_text: A sage-green notebook cover with a dark green binding stitched in cream down its left edge. Under the headline Name: Mummy., a printed school label with notched corners and a double border is filled in by hand: Std., every one, twice. Subject, herself, for once. Roll no., 1. Below it lies the real bracelet, a fine gold tone chain with small satellite beads and two heart-shaped clear stones set side by side as a bow, over the line mummy's bow, minus the tug. At the foot: Naira, Mangal, and mangal in Telugu script, beside a small almirah key.

deviations: GRID PASS r1 (26 Oct). 'shown larger.' deleted (it stood at right edge ~890, baseline ~1060): against the notebook label the bracelet is about life size, so the note was untrue. build.py's note parameter is now None.

GRID PASS r1. The new seal (sage, మంగళ one copy in oxblood at 30 px, MANGAL 64 in oxblood with a 2 px marigold plate, wordmark-oxblood at 120 px, chaabi-seal-sage with OXBLOOD petals: a sage cut-out vanished in the light steel). build.py now writes it from _system/_build/seal.py into the template's __SEAL__ slot (it used to copy the script line from partials/seal.html); s01 and s01-fallback-mr were regenerated (python3 _build/build.py s01; python3 _build/build.py s01-fallback-mr '{"script":"mr"}') and differ from the previous files only in the note and the seal. Measured ink box on both: x 389.5-693, y 1235-1364.5 (303.5 x 129.5, centre x 541.2).

Real photo, re-cut: the spec's cutouts/ribbon-bead-bracelet/00-trim.png comes from the listing's GENERATED still life (hf_20260809_164607, assets 04.png). Checked at 4x it shows a spring-ring clasp and no extender (the real piece has a lobster clasp and an extender ring: assets 02.jpg = Shopify ribbon-bead-bracelet-0), its gold reads rose (median hue 27 deg against the real photo's 32 deg), and its binary matte kept plaster in the soft back links. Never-list 12 and 23 (no clasp the listing photos do not show, no substituted parts) decided it. The piece is now cut from the real product photograph: BiRefNet on the plinth-top crop (_build/cut_real.py, run locally on assets/shopify/ribbon-bead-bracelet/02.jpg rather than tools/cut_one.py, which matte the whole frame where the plaster cube becomes the subject), then _build/refine_real.py: BiRefNet's edge for everything in focus (it leaves out the chain's warm cast shadow), plaster removed from inside the links, a yellowness difference key for the soft-focus back of the loop so it stays continuous, small highlight holes filled, the bow's claw shadow cleared, and every part-transparent pixel un-mixed from the local plaster colour. Output p09/assets/ribbon-real-trim.png (801x414). Art-director fix of 25 Oct, a residue pass in the same script: cream plaster was left on the sharp front chain right of the bow (a crescent under and left of the satellite bead, and inside the open links) and pale and cyan flecks on the top-right back run. Now (1) on the front chain right of the bow, a pixel pale (L > .78) and weakly saturated (s under .28, the key fading out by .36, where the lit gold sits), in the photograph or as it would display once un-mixed, goes to alpha 0; (2) on the soft back only what would display near-white, or cool (blue >= green), goes; (3) specular cores are spared: yellow-white or neutral, brighter than any plaster, and held by BiRefNet (bir > .5) in focus or enclosed by the matte on the back, so the bead's highlight, the clasp's glints and the links' glints stay, while lit-plaster specks that pass for glints (bir 0-.13) go; (4) each satellite bead's highlight, which the old cut had left as a hole showing the ground through the bead, is filled; the left bead's lit side is raised to BiRefNet's alpha; (5) a bead's dark band (un-mixed to black, a navy dot) is opaque; (6) on the back, pinholes the key leaves inside the metal are closed and coloured from the gold around them. (25 Oct: the strict front key ran only right of the bow; see 26 Oct, item 3, for the left.) Residue audit on the trim (alpha > .15, outside the bow): pale 924 px to 7, cool 301 to 5, near-black 233 to 2, all single pixels, sub-pixel at 0.824. The crop is now pinned to the 801x414 box the layout was measured on, so the cleaner matte does not change the display scale. Before/after at 4-6x on sage and oxblood: _work/fix25-crescent-before-after.png, fix25-backrun-before-after.png, fix25-clasp-before-after.png, fix25-leftbead-before-after.png (previous trim kept as _work/ribbon-real-trim-before-fix25.png). The back of the loop is soft because the photograph is; it was kept soft, not sharpened or redrawn. The spec's x00 route (cut_one.py ribbon-bead-bracelet 0) names the same photograph. ART-DIRECTOR FIX PASS OF 26 OCT, same script (rules 7-12), trim still pinned to 801x414 and placed as before (box 222/736, 660x341.1, -10 deg; every pixel that changed on the render lies inside x 238-851, y 741-1072). (1) Extender ring RESTORED. The 25 Oct back-run rule (2) had deleted its lit metal (pale yellow-white, v .97-1.00, hue 38-66) and left two horns. Inside a 26 px disc round the ring (feathered to 30), the cut now uses BiRefNet's own alpha and the un-mixed colour, taking out only plain plaster (pink cream, hue 19-35, no brighter than the plaster round it). BiRefNet had kept that plaster in the upper half of the ring's hole at .9, so removing it gives a closed O with its hole open to the ground, as in 02.jpg. The disc is centred on the middle of the ring's outer edge, trim (617,66) (box x 595-640, y 43-88). The AD's 'about (620,55)' is near the hole, which perspective puts up and right of the centre; a disc there left the ring's lit lower-left arc, 28 px out, still cut. The four soft links from the ring to the right-hand back bead had been thinned by the same rule into a broken thread, so the ring's treatment also runs along them in a 13 px corridor: the extender now reads ring, links, bead, as in the photograph. (2) Back-run beads: each had lost its lit upper-left quarter (hue 35-60, BiRefNet .9) and read as a star. In a 12 px disc round each, warm pale pixels and the rule (a) white cores (the second bead's centre is hue 59-66, s .07) are spared, raised to BiRefNet's alpha with a 1.4 px soft edge, and any hole is filled. The discs are centred on the beads as measured, trim (68,111) and (231,42), so they hold the highlights at x 58-66 and 223-231; a disc at the AD's (75,110) would miss the first. Then a 1.5 px (3x3) grey opening on the back-run alpha only, outside the ring, corridor and bead discs: features under 3 px wide went from 36 px, reaching 5 px out from the chain, to 1 px reaching 1 px, and none reaches past 4 px. The defocus ramps are monotone and pass through unchanged. (3) Front chain left of the bow: target NOT met, deliberately. The strict front key was run there as asked (16 px disc round the left bead and the stones' hull excluded). It does bring the pale share to 11.6%, but it removes 28% of the run's opaque pixels and leaves the links as barbs (_work/fix26-leftchain-strictkey-tried.png). The pale pixels are not plaster. On this side the light comes from the upper left and each link's outer face is lit, a pale yellow-white ring in the photograph itself (hue 40-60 against the plaster's pink 19-35, and far from it in colour; _work/fix26/z-links10.png). Measured on the same footprint, the photograph is 35.5% pale by the AD's measure on the left and 2.0% on the right, so the asymmetry belongs to the photograph. What was actually wrong there is fixed. The rim-sparing rule that held every link's mixed edge pixel at full weight now runs only inside the left bead's disc. Alpha is BiRefNet's own smooth edge eased onto a 1-2 px ramp, where the colour keys had left it ragged and speckled white on dark grounds. Every plaster-like pixel (pink or mauve cream, unsaturated) goes, which opens the link holes: plaster-hued pixels held there fell from 96 to 57. The pale share moves from 34.0% to 35.2%, with the rings whole and their edge clean. Tighter ramps were tried and stayed at about 35%, which confirms the pale pixels are the links' lit body, not their edge. The stones' hull is the convex hull of BiRefNet's mask opened by 8 px, plus the left stone's top prong, grown 2 px (_work/fix26/hull-convex8.png); a tighter outline let the plaster test take the clear stone's tip, which was seen and corrected. (4a) The upper right bead's highlight is now kept as metal (7 px disc, BiRefNet's alpha, soft edge), so there is no notch. (4b) Under the front-right links (trim x 330-420, y 360-395) nothing stands above BiRefNet's alpha, and nothing stands where BiRefNet has none: 232 px of pink cast-shadow smudge went to 0. Also removed: a near-black hairline under the left stone's collar (part-alpha pixels that un-mixed to black). Residue audit on the trim (_build/audit_residue.py: alpha > .15, outside the stones; pale = displays near-white, L > .86 and s < .18; cool = blue >= green - .01; near-black = max channel < .15), old trim against new, same masks: outside the places where the photograph's own light is pale, pale fell from 20 to 6 (the lit edge of one extender link), cool from 10 to 1 and near-black from 2 to 0. Pale in total rises from 728 to 1650, because restored metal is pale by nature: the ring and its links 645, the back beads' highlights 163, the left run's lit faces 542, specular cores 254, the right bead's highlight 40. Before/after at 4x on sage and oxblood (photo | BiRefNet | before | after, on sage then on oxblood): _work/fix26-ring-before-after.png, fix26-extender-links-before-after.png, fix26-backbeads-before-after.png, fix26-leftchain-before-after.png, fix26-notch-before-after.png, fix26-shadow-before-after.png; on the final render: _work/fix26-render-ring-4x.png, -beads-4x, -leftchain-4x, -shadow-4x. Previous trim kept as _work/fix26/trim-before-fix26.png.

Placement follows the real photo: it shows the loop in three-quarter view with the bow at the lower left, so it is turned -10 deg to bring the bow to the front of the loop, shown at 660x341.1 (0.824 of native) with its box at left 222, top 736 (art director, 25 Oct; was 262 / 722). Measured on the render: ink spans x 238-867, y 735-1077, centre x 552, inside the label's 190-890 above it; label to clasp 45 px, bracelet ink to the aside's ascenders 42 px; the contact shadow has faded by y 1116, above the aside's ascenders at 1118. The box height now comes from the trim's own size (414, not the 415 build.py had, a 0.24% vertical stretch). Spec: the other matte at 546x388 centred on (540,906).

Setup line dropped ('every june, she wrote our names on everything.'): the system allows ONE Cormorant aside per cover and the spec carried two; the spec's own fallback is 'drop the setup line first'. The punchline that explains the bracelet ('mummy's bow, minus the tug.') stays; the setup's idea opens the caption, and the label itself tells it.

SUPERSEDED (grid pass r1: 'shown larger.' deleted): 'shown larger.' added (Cormorant italic 28, plum, right-aligned at x 890, baseline 1060; art director, 25 Oct: was right edge 1000, baseline 1046, past every other right edge on the tile): system device 4 applies to any cut-out enlarged on a drawn object.
